statement: Drug effect follows a sigmoid dose-response curve; the therapeutic index (toxic dose / effective dose) separates forgiving wide-TI drugs from narrow-TI drugs where small PK changes flip therapeutic to toxic.
effect_size: Narrow-TI examples (warfarin, digoxin, lithium, phenytoin, aminoglycosides) have toxic and effective concentrations nearly overlapping

provenance.primary: Goodman & Gilman's Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 14th ed.; Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology

confidence_notes: Foundational pharmacodynamics. Same dose-response logic as hormesis (section 01 §3). Narrow-TI status is the single best predictor of where interactions and PGx matter.

statement: Orally administered drugs pass through the liver via the portal vein before systemic circulation (first-pass effect), which can metabolize a large fraction and lowers oral bioavailability relative to IV (100%).
effect_size: Peptides (insulin) have near-zero oral bioavailability; many drugs need far larger oral than IV doses

provenance.primary: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology; Rowland & Tozer Clinical Pharmacokinetics

confidence_notes: Explains why route matters (sublingual/transdermal/inhaled bypass first-pass) and why peptide drugs like GLP-1s are injected.

statement: The cytochrome P450 family (chiefly CYP3A4/5, 2D6, 2C19, 2C9) performs most Phase-I drug metabolism; CYP inhibition raises substrate levels (toxicity) and CYP induction lowers them (loss of effect), making this the dominant drug-interaction mechanism.
effect_size: CYP3A4 metabolizes ~half of all metabolized drugs; St. John's Wort (CYP3A4/P-gp inducer) has caused transplant rejection and contraceptive failure
population: General pharmacology; documented case series for inducer interactions

provenance.primary: Lynch & Price, Am Fam Physician 2007 (CYP450 review); Goodman & Gilman 14th ed.

confidence_notes: Mechanism is settled; specific interaction magnitudes vary. Protein-binding-displacement interactions are real but often overstated vs metabolic ones.

statement: For an active drug, a poor-metabolizer genotype causes accumulation/toxicity; for a prodrug (codeine, clopidogrel) the same poor-metabolizer genotype causes therapeutic failure, while an ultrarapid metabolizer causes dangerous over-activation.
effect_size: CYP2D6 activity ranges from zero (gene deletion) to ultrarapid (gene duplication); codeine ultrarapid metabolizers have had fatal morphine toxicity
population: General PGx principle; documented codeine deaths (FDA boxed warning)

provenance.primary: Crews et al., CPIC CYP2D6/opioid guideline, Clin Pharmacol Ther 2021

confidence_notes: The conceptual crux of pharmacogenomics. The inversion explains why genotype direction-of-effect depends on whether the drug is a prodrug.

statement: CYP2C19 loss-of-function carriers cannot fully activate the prodrug clopidogrel, getting less antiplatelet protection after stenting/ACS; guidelines recommend an alternative antiplatelet (prasugrel/ticagrelor).
effect_size: LoF carriers have higher stent thrombosis / ischemic events; genotype-guided therapy (TAILOR-PCI direction) favors alternatives in carriers
population: PCI/ACS patients; LoF alleles common in East-Asian ancestry

provenance.primary: Lee et al., CPIC clopidogrel/CYP2C19 guideline 2022

confidence_notes: One of the strongest actionable gene-drug pairs; trial direction (TAILOR-PCI) supportive though formal superiority was modest. Extends section 18.

statement: Codeine and tramadol are CYP2D6-activated prodrugs: ultrarapid metabolizers risk life-threatening opioid toxicity (including infant deaths via breast milk) and poor metabolizers get no analgesia; both should avoid these opioids.
effect_size: Documented fatal/near-fatal toxicity in ultrarapid metabolizers; FDA boxed warning and contraindication in children
population: Pediatric and breastfeeding case series; CYP2D6 phenotype groups

provenance.primary: Crews et al., CPIC CYP2D6/opioid guideline, Clin Pharmacol Ther 2021

confidence_notes: PGx with a body count; among the few PGx applications that are unequivocally life-saving. Evidence is case-series + mechanism, not RCT, but causally clear.

statement: CYP2C9 and VKORC1 genotypes explain a large share of inter-individual warfarin dose variance and inform genotype-guided starting doses, but genotype-guided dosing's outcome benefit over standard INR-guided care is mixed.
effect_size: Genotype + clinical factors explain ~40-50% of dose variance; trials (COAG vs EU-PACT) gave conflicting outcome results

provenance.primary: Johnson et al., CPIC CYP2C9/VKORC1 warfarin guideline, Clin Pharmacol Ther 2017

confidence_notes: Dose-prediction value is strong; clinical-outcome superiority over good INR monitoring is genuinely contested (COAG null, EU-PACT positive). Honest 'mixed' on outcomes, strong on dosing.

statement: TPMT or NUDT15 deficiency prevents inactivation of thiopurines (azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine), causing life-threatening myelosuppression at standard doses; pre-treatment testing with dose reduction/avoidance is standard of care.
effect_size: Homozygous-deficient patients face severe/fatal bone-marrow toxicity at conventional doses; dose reduced drastically or drug avoided

provenance.primary: Relling et al., CPIC TPMT/NUDT15 thiopurine guideline update, Clin Pharmacol Ther 2019

confidence_notes: Classic test-before-treat PGx; strong, established, prevents catastrophe. Mary Relling's lab central to this guideline.

statement: DPYD deficiency prevents clearance of fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy (5-FU, capecitabine), causing severe or fatal toxicity; pre-treatment DPYD testing is now standard in much of Europe.
effect_size: DPYD-variant carriers have markedly higher severe-toxicity and treatment-death risk; pre-emptive dose reduction reduces it (prospective Henricks 2018 cohort)

provenance.primary: CPIC DPYD/fluoropyrimidine guideline; Henricks et al., Lancet Oncol 2018 prospective DPYD-guided dosing

confidence_notes: Pre-emptive single-gene testing that demonstrably saves lives; adopted as standard in EU. Among the strongest cases for pre-treatment PGx.

statement: Single HLA alleles predict severe drug hypersensitivity: HLA-B*57:01 for abacavir (near-100% negative predictive value, mandatory testing) and HLA-B*15:02 for carbamazepine-induced Stevens-Johnson syndrome in at-risk ancestries.
effect_size: PREDICT-1 RCT: HLA-B*57:01 screening eliminated immunologically-confirmed abacavir hypersensitivity
population: HIV patients (abacavir); epilepsy/neuropathy patients of Southeast/East-Asian ancestry (carbamazepine)

provenance.primary: Mallal et al., NEJM 2008 (PREDICT-1); CPIC HLA guidelines

confidence_notes: Abacavir/HLA-B*57:01 is RCT-grade and mandatory; the cleanest 'genetics with a body count, prevented by a cheap test' example.

statement: Broad combinatorial 'psychiatric pharmacogenomic' panels marketed to pick antidepressants show small, short-lived effects at best and no durable improvement in remission in large pragmatic trials.
effect_size: PRIME Care (VA, JAMA 2022): genotype-guided prescribing modestly reduced predicted drug-gene interactions but no durable remission benefit
population: Veterans with major depression starting/switching antidepressants

provenance.primary: Oslin et al., JAMA 2022 (PRIME Care)

confidence_notes: Honesty counterweight: single-gene high-stakes PGx is strong; broad consumer 'DNA picks your drug' psychiatric panels run ahead of evidence. Not a conflict in mechanism, a conflict in marketing claims.

statement: Grapefruit juice irreversibly inhibits intestinal CYP3A4 (via furanocoumarins), raising blood levels of CYP3A4-substrate drugs as if a larger dose were taken; the effect lasts 24+ hours and matters most for narrow-TI substrates.
effect_size: Dozens of documented interacting drugs (some statins, calcium-channel blockers, immunosuppressants); some statin levels rise several-fold

provenance.primary: Bailey DG et al., CMAJ 2013 (Grapefruit-medication interactions)

confidence_notes: Clean everyday demonstration that a food is a drug interaction and 'natural' confers no safety. Magnitude varies by drug and individual gut CYP3A4.

statement: Polypharmacy (often defined as >=5 medications) compounds interaction risk combinatorially in older adults, who also have altered PK/PD; deprescribing inappropriate medications is frequently the highest-value pharmacological intervention.
effect_size: Polypharmacy associated with falls, delirium, hospitalization; prescribing cascades a leading reversible cause; Beers/STOPP-START operationalize deprescribing

provenance.primary: AGS Beers Criteria (J Am Geriatr Soc, updated periodically); STOPP/START criteria

confidence_notes: Associations are cohort-grade (confounding by indication/frailty); the deprescribing principle is consensus-guideline. Anticholinergic burden has a dementia-association signal (cohort).

statement: Supplements have a real, frequently-ignored drug-interaction surface: St. John's Wort (CYP3A4/P-gp induction -> transplant rejection, contraceptive failure), vitamin K/fish oil/ginkgo with anticoagulants, and mineral/antacid chelation blocking antibiotic/thyroid absorption.
effect_size: St. John's Wort documented to cause transplant rejection and contraceptive/HIV/anticoagulant drug failure via induction
population: General; documented case reports and PK studies

provenance.primary: Izzo & Ernst, Drugs 2009 (herb-drug interactions review); St. John's Wort case literature

confidence_notes: 'Natural' predicts nothing about interaction risk. Compounded by supplement quality/regulation gaps making contents (and thus interactions) unpredictable.

statement: Placebo analgesia is a real neurobiological effect partly mediated by endogenous opioids and reversible by naloxone; placebo responses have their own dose-response (ritual, route, price) and exist even in open-label form.
effect_size: Naloxone blocks placebo analgesia (Levine 1978); open-label placebo produced symptom benefit in IBS (Kaptchuk 2010)
population: Pain and symptom-based conditions (pain, IBS, fatigue, Parkinson's)

provenance.primary: Levine, Gordon & Fields, Lancet 1978 (naloxone-reversible placebo); Kaptchuk et al., PLoS ONE 2010 (open-label placebo IBS)

confidence_notes: Real endogenous pharmacology, modest magnitude, studied in symptom-based not curative contexts. The reason RCTs need placebo arms and 'it worked for me' is the weakest tier.

statement: Negative expectation (nocebo) produces real adverse symptoms, drives much reported drug intolerance, and causes excess side-effect reporting when patients switch to generics or are warned of effects.
effect_size: SAMSON n-of-1: ~90% of 'statin side effects' occurred on placebo months too; documented nocebo barrier to generic switching

provenance.primary: Wood et al., NEJM 2020 (SAMSON)

confidence_notes: Nocebo is clinically expensive (non-adherence). Cross-references the section-10 statin nocebo finding; central to the generic=brand honesty (F.1).

statement: Generic drugs must prove bioequivalence (90% CI of generic/brand AUC and Cmax ratio within 80-125%), are the same active drug, and are not weaker or lower quality; narrow-TI drugs warrant product consistency and nocebo explains much 'generic doesn't work' reporting.
effect_size: Meta-analyses (e.g. Kesselheim JAMA 2008, cardiovascular generics) found no clinically significant difference in outcomes vs brand

provenance.primary: Kesselheim et al., JAMA 2008 (clinical equivalence of generic vs brand cardiovascular drugs); FDA Orange Book bioequivalence standard

confidence_notes: Bioequivalence window is a CI around the mean, so averages typically within a few percent. Honest caveats: narrow-TI consistency, rare excipient intolerance, nocebo.

statement: 'Natural' describes origin, not safety, efficacy, or dose, and predicts none of them; the same questions (does it work, at what dose, with what harms and interactions) apply identically to plant extracts and synthesized molecules.
effect_size: Digitalis, warfarin, botulinum toxin, ricin, aflatoxin, St. John's Wort, grapefruit are all 'natural'

provenance.primary: Toxicology/pharmacology consensus (Paracelsus dose-makes-the-poison; herb-drug interaction literature)

confidence_notes: The supplement-side twin of the mechanism-not-outcome rule. Strong as a logical/toxicological point; framed as hypothesis-grade because it is a framing claim, not an effect estimate.

statement: US supplements are regulated under DSHEA (1994) as a food-like category not required to prove safety or efficacy before sale; independent testing repeatedly finds mislabeled contents, wrong species, and undeclared pharmaceutical adulterants.
effect_size: FDA recall record documents hidden sildenafil analogs, sibutramine, and steroids; DNA-barcoding studies found mislabeled herbal species

provenance.primary: DSHEA 1994; FDA tainted-products database; Newmaster et al. BMC Med 2013 (herbal DNA barcoding)

confidence_notes: Regulation gap is documented fact; quality varies widely. Third-party certification (USP/NSF/Informed Choice) is the only real signal of contents. Cross-ref section 03.

statement: Most drug candidates fail (mostly in Phase II/III for lack of efficacy); aggregate R&D cost is high largely because of those failures, and a drug's price tracks market exclusivity/patents, not manufacturing or R&D cost.
effect_size: ~$1-2.6B per approved drug (DiMasi, capitalized incl. failures) is contested; collapse to near-free price at generic entry shows price tracks exclusivity not cost

provenance.primary: DiMasi et al., J Health Econ 2016 (contested cost estimate); generic-entry price literature

confidence_notes: The cost figure is advocacy-laden and contested (out-of-pocket far lower than capitalized). 'Mixed' because the headline numbers serve different arguments; the price-tracks-exclusivity point is robust.

statement: For chronic non-cancer pain (back/osteoarthritis), opioids are not superior to non-opioid regimens over 12 months (slightly worse), at the cost of dependence and overdose risk; opioids remain valuable for acute, post-surgical, and cancer/palliative pain.
effect_size: SPACE RCT: opioids no better (slightly worse pain-related function) than non-opioid therapy at 12 months
population: 240 patients with chronic back or hip/knee OA pain (SPACE)

provenance.primary: Krebs et al., JAMA 2018 (SPACE)

confidence_notes: Decisive negative against opioids as first-line for chronic non-cancer pain. Mechanism (mu-opioid agonism) real; the honest framing is the net ledger. Cross-ref sections 21 and 14.

statement: NSAIDs (COX inhibitors) carry real, common harms beyond their reputation: GI ulcers/bleeding (COX-1), acute kidney injury (especially the ACEi/ARB + diuretic 'triple whammy'), blood-pressure elevation, and a cardiovascular-event signal with chronic high-dose use.
effect_size: NSAIDs among leading causes of drug-induced GI bleeds and AKI; CNT meta-analysis showed CV-event excess with high-dose non-aspirin NSAIDs
population: General; older adults at highest risk

provenance.primary: Coxib and traditional NSAID Trialists' (CNT) Collaboration, Lancet 2013

confidence_notes: NSAIDs are not the benign default they are treated as; harm concentrates in older adults, dehydration, CKD, heart failure, and with anticoagulants. Cross-ref section 21.

statement: Acetaminophen is safe at therapeutic dose and lacks NSAID GI/renal/CV harms, but in overdose its metabolite NAPQI overwhelms glutathione and destroys the liver, making it a leading cause of acute liver failure; risk is amplified by alcohol/fasting and by its presence in combination products.
effect_size: Leading cause of acute liver failure in the US/UK; N-acetylcysteine antidote effective if given early

provenance.primary: Larson et al., Hepatology 2005 (acetaminophen-induced acute liver failure); standard toxicology

confidence_notes: A narrow-TI lesson hiding in the most ordinary OTC drug; the margin is narrow and the drug is hidden in combination cold/flu products.
